topic: tenant law; forged document; informal justice
direct_evidence: Law protects tenant paying one-third crop tax; landlord forges a document; Brotherhood later coerces farmers; narrator remains indebted to landlord.
comparative_use: Law can exist yet be bypassed; counter-justice can reproduce coercion.
caveat: One character narrative; cross-reference to Vlandian research, not independent population evidence.

direct_evidence: Illegitimate child expects no inheritance; neighbors fund a substitute for royal levy; captive released on promise to pay later.
comparative_use: Military service can be community-financed and debt-mediated rather than land-rewarded.
caveat: Do not infer a universal levy law.

topic: land scarcity; urban labor; gang coercion
direct_evidence: Land shortage moves younger sons to docks; war displaces landholders; gangs control hiring and kill a worker's brother.
comparative_use: War restructures labor markets and produces non-state coercion.

topic: frontier identity; rejection of serf status
direct_evidence: Northwestern residents reject treatment as serfs and relocate after a bailiff insults their father.
comparative_use: Regional identity and frontier risk complicate uniform peasant-status models.
caveat: Local status claim, not proof that dependency is absent.

direct_evidence: A lord considers hanging a violent retainer; a witness's words may determine whether he lives.
comparative_use: Formal authority can punish, but outcomes are discretionary and witness-dependent.
caveat: Soldier's moralized account, not a court record.

direct_evidence: Raiding wealth buys land and thralls; the next generation plans to bring home silver and slaves to buy land for the family.
comparative_use: Land accumulation can be financed through raiding and slave-taking.
caveat: Do not generalize to all Sturgians.

direct_evidence: A fence dispute leads to a killing; the narrator offers blood money, then kills two more after a relative lays hands on him; unable to pay for three deaths, he flees.
comparative_use: Customary compensation exists but can fail after escalation and kin violence.
caveat: No empire-wide blood-money tariff can be inferred.

direct_evidence: An orphan says his sister's husband hires a skilled legal advocate and wins part of the parents' farm in court/council.
comparative_use: Formal adjudication exists, but procedural expertise may create unequal outcomes.
caveat: Narrator cannot reproduce the argument; corruption is not independently proven.

direct_evidence: Elders recognize a duel as fair and not murder, yet the woman is excluded from the deceased's inheritance.
comparative_use: Legal recognition of conduct does not guarantee inheritance or material autonomy.
caveat: One story does not establish uniform gender law.

topic: land; tenants; local defense; kin conflict
direct_evidence: A land- and cattle-rich stepfather sends a youth and tenants to hold a ford; the narrator later says he was intentionally sent to die amid family rivalry.
comparative_use: Landholding families can mobilize tenants for defense while using military assignments for internal power struggles.
caveat: Intentional betrayal is a narrator's accusation.

topic: skill labor; service; broken reward promise
direct_evidence: A horse trainer promised a horse after three years' service is offered only a goat after the lord gives the herd to his son.
comparative_use: Patronage and service do not guarantee enforceable compensation.
caveat: The text mentions fen Uvain; companion numeric ID alone does not supply a culture field.

direct_evidence: A village peddler says steppe elites tax villagers, trample crops and take people to war; he plans to flee to a group outside the khan's authority.
comparative_use: Village production and war obligations can be experienced as extractive domination; alternative affiliation exists.
caveat: Grievance narrative, not a neutral tax description.

topic: expulsion; forced sale; land and slaves
direct_evidence: After social expulsion from an encampment, a family sells land and slaves for a fraction of their value and is later raided.
comparative_use: Property insecurity can arise from community exclusion and raiding, not only state policy.
caveat: Do not attribute the expulsion to the khan without evidence.

topic: slavery; arena law; elite exception; manumission
direct_evidence: An enslaved gladiator says imperial law bans killing in public arenas while private elite entertainments escape scrutiny; winnings eventually buy freedom.
comparative_use: Formal law and elite private practice can diverge; slavery and manumission cross cultural boundaries.
caveat: 3Yax10rQ has no archived official CN key; template ID does not establish full origin or social system.

direct_evidence: A slave's son is educated with a judge's sons but lacks capital and client networks to become a physician.
comparative_use: Household access does not equal legal freedom or equal occupational opportunity.
caveat: One household story, not a complete account of Aserai slavery.

topic: community protector; state coercion; local trust
direct_evidence: An alley protector refuses a guard captain's demands to cover an abduction and spy on residents; the captain threatens his father and he flees.
comparative_use: Local legitimacy and formal state authority can conflict; neither is automatically just.
caveat: A local role in one town, not a universal institution.

topic: kinship summons; military service; no fiefs
direct_evidence: A minor clan with no fiefs or wealth still answers when kin or the Sultan summons it.
comparative_use: Military obligation need not be grounded in landholding or guarantee land reward.
caveat: A clan's self-description, not a full mobilization record.

direct_evidence: Most inheritance goes to brothers; the daughter must earn quickly to be treated as equal, then loses her capital in a warehouse fire and faces gendered mockery.
comparative_use: Inheritance and market status can remain unequal even when a woman manages family business.
caveat: Gepa1szA has no archived official CN key and is reused in companion_strings.xml; not independent corroboration.

direct_evidence: A lord's great-niece is expected to marry a horseman in his retinue but falls in love with a common soldier.
comparative_use: Military households reproduce rank through marriage expectations as well as service.
caveat: Culture is inferred from Sarghert/Aldric references, not from an explicit culture field.
